clue.text: Having a hunch, and seeing bore after golf maybe

indicators.note: placed after says the word for bore follows the golf word

parts.note: a round is a game of golf, one example of a round in sport
bore as a past tense of bear, carrying a load on one's shoulders, means shouldered

explanation.surface: Someone with a hunch watches a dull person turn up after a game of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunch' suggests an intuition, but it is the stoop of the back; 'bore' looks like a dull person but is the verb carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunched posture, shoulders curving forward, is exactly what having a hunch describes literally.

clue.text: With page missing, took it as read and carried on

indicators.note: missing means the page letter is taken away

parts.note: to take something as read is to presume it

explanation.surface: Someone skipped a missing page, assumed what it said, and carried on.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to continue after a pause, so resumed means carried on.

clue.text: Marriage may see us now in obvious need initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A couple's marriage, they now see, is an obvious need.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining together, and marriage is the union of two people.

clue.text: Political manipulator some gauged criminal having lost son

indicators.note: criminal means the letters are treated badly and scrambled
having lost says a letter for son is taken out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A political manipulator is accused of some criminal act after losing his son.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S from SOME GAUGED and rearrange the remaining OMEGAUGED.
explanation.definitionFit: A demagogue is a leader who wins support by playing on popular prejudice, a political manipulator.

clue.text: Run quickly to cover case of affair in capital

indicators.note: covering means the running word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to hare is to run very fast

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters, here of affair

explanation.surface: Someone runs quickly through the capital to cover up an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Harare is the capital city of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Rocky could be nude, say, dancing around top of table

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
dancing means the letters move about into a new order
the top of a down word is its first letter, here of table

explanation.surface: A naked dancer on a tabletop makes it rocky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is part of the fodder, not a signal that the nude is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rocky wobbles and is not firmly fixed, i.e. unsteady.

clue.text: Performers to be paid on time?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting on top, so the payment word comes first

parts.note: money due is money owed, to be paid

explanation.surface: Asking whether performers will be paid on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is a pair of performers, two musicians or singers together.

clue.text: Echoed editor supporting soldiers with short composition

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed below, so the editor goes at the bottom

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: short means the composition loses its final letter

parts.note: a sonata is a musical composition for an instrument

explanation.surface: An editor backs soldiers who wrote a brief piece of music that echoed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that resonated rang out and reverberated, as an echo does.

clue.text: Heartlessly deny repulsive ruling family

indicators.note: without its heart means the middle letters of deny are dropped, keeping its ends

parts.note: nasty means repulsive

explanation.surface: A cruel denial that a repulsive ruling family exists.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of rulers from the same family.

clue.text: Start to hope lancing boil and shine

indicators.note: lancing pierces something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to boil gently is to simmer

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here taken from hope

explanation.surface: A medical picture: lancing a boil, hoping it will heal and the skin will shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boil' reads as a skin swelling, but it is the verb, cooking gently.
explanation.definitionFit: A shimmer is a soft wavering gleam, a kind of shine.

clue.text: Family member's crushes?

definitions.meaning: a relative by a parent's marriage, a spouse's son
to crush is to tread down on, split as two words 5,2

explanation.surface: A question about which relative a family member has a crush on.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer 5,2 for the second sense; 'crushes' looks like infatuations but is the verb tread on.
explanation.definitionFit: A son of one's spouse from an earlier marriage is a family member, and treading down hard on something crushes it.

clue.text: Caged animals finding endless grief after people grow old

indicators.note: after puts the shortened grief following the other pieces

parts.note: men means people in a general sense
to age is to grow old

indicators.note: without its ends means both outside letters of grief are dropped

explanation.surface: Sorrow at caged animals growing old in captivity.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept in cages for exhibition.

clue.text: Responsibility of star making a comeback after Oscar

indicators.note: after places the turned star following the Oscar letter

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: coming back means the word for star is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the sun is our nearest star

explanation.surface: A film star's comeback after winning an Oscar brings responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' and 'Oscar' suggest the film world, but the star is in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty that falls to someone, a responsibility.

clue.text: Torrent of water from river covering lounge, oddly

indicators.note: covering means the river word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in odd positions, first, third and fifth, of lounge

explanation.surface: A river flood pours water into someone's lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee flows in Scotland and on the Welsh border; LUG comes from the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is a great flood or heavy downpour, a torrent of water.

clue.text: Starts off breaking regulation — that's the limit!

indicators.note: breaking into means the jumbled letters split the regulation word

parts.note: a law is a regulation

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone starts breaking the rules and an exasperated voice declares enough is enough.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straw, from the straw that broke the camel's back, is the final provocation beyond which one cannot tolerate more.

clue.text: Lay out, protecting right in France with skill

indicators.note: protecting means the rearranged letters surround and shield the French word
out here means put out of order, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: droit is French for right

explanation.surface: Laying someone out skilfully, while defending a right in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay out' looks like a phrase meaning knock down, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something adroitly means doing it deftly, with skill.

clue.text: Hospitality to begin with hotel on river

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting on top, so the river comes below

parts.note: to open is to begin
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A riverside hotel offering hospitality from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, among several English rivers of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping open house means welcoming all visitors, a generous form of hospitality.

clue.text: Cancel summons seeing upper-class type swallow drug

indicators.note: swallowing means the drug letter goes inside the upper-class word

parts.note: a writ is a legal summons
a toff is a slang word for a posh person; its T has to be shared with the summons word for the letters to fit
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A posh person swallows drugs and a court summons gets cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is flawed: WRIT plus TOFF with E inside gives one T too many. The fit works only if the two words share the T, as the Big Dave blog also notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To write off a debt is to cancel it as unrecoverable.

clue.text: Freely rely on army accommodation here

indicators.note: on means the rearranged letters come next to the army word

parts.note: a host is an army, a great multitude

indicators.note: freely means the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Rely on the army to provide accommodation freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army' is the old sense of host, as in heavenly host; the definition says this is where you would find accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an inn or pub, a place offering lodging to travellers.

clue.text: Boxer born in shack gets fish

indicators.note: in puts the boxer and born letters inside the shack word

parts.note: a hut is a shack
Muhammad Ali was a famous boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer born in a humble shack ends up with a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish of northern seas.

clue.text: Tunnellers sent back across Germany rarely

indicators.note: across means the moles word stretches over the Germany letter
sent back means the whole is read in reverse

parts.note: moles are animals that tunnel underground
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Tunnellers rarely get sent back across the German border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tunnellers' suggest wartime escapers, but they are the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom is an adverb meaning not often, a synonym of rarely.

clue.text: Working during early spring for sovereign

indicators.note: during means the working word sits within the month

parts.note: March is a month early in spring
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A sovereign working through early spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' could be the gold coin, but it is the ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a king or queen, a sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Tabloid with dislike mostly for high-level protection

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to hate is to dislike strongly

explanation.surface: A tabloid with a grudge seeks protection at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid daily; 'high-level' refers to the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunhat protects the head, the highest part of the body, from the sun.

clue.text: Rich type who drinks a lot

definitions.meaning: rich means luxuriant, of vegetation growing thickly
a heavy drinker, an alcoholic in slang

explanation.surface: A wealthy person who is also a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush means luxuriant or rich, and as slang a lush is a heavy drinker.

clue.text: Contact head of development with private land

parts.note: to touch is to make contact

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here from development

parts.note: own means belonging privately to one

explanation.surface: A developer gets in contact about a plot of private land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like the property noun but is the verb, as an aircraft does.
explanation.definitionFit: When an aircraft lands it makes touchdown, reaching the ground.

clue.text: Outstanding old extension

parts.note: a wing is an extension built onto a building

explanation.surface: An old building's extension stands out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means excellent on the surface, but here it means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is owing is outstanding, still to be paid.

clue.text: Level achieved by heartless golfer?

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the golfer's name is removed

parts.note: Tiger Woods is a famous golfer

explanation.surface: A golfer without heart achieves a certain level.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or rank, as in rows of seats one above another.

clue.text: Tex-Mex food — it will be eaten by donkey

indicators.note: being eaten by puts the word it inside the donkey word

parts.note: a burro is a small donkey, a Spanish word used in the US Southwest

explanation.surface: A donkey will happily eat Tex-Mex food.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly the dish's name means little donkey in Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a flour tortilla wrapped round a filling, a staple of Tex-Mex cooking.

clue.text: The lady's bringing in gold left with international trucker

indicators.note: bringing in means the other letters go inside the lady word

parts.note: the lady's means belonging to her
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A woman brings in gold, having left with an international lorry driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A haulier is a person or firm that carries goods by road, a trucker.

clue.text: Sadly forget North-West must find great support

indicators.note: sadly here means in a sorry state, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who forgot about the North-West must find a great backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower of strength is an idiom for a person who gives steadfast support in hard times.
